Sorting records by two keys

42

I am collecting records by date, and I want to sort them by the timestamp first and use a stable name comparison to break ties. The records can receive the same timestamp, especially when a batch arrives together.

My current implementation uses two independent sorts. What is the simplest way to express the order with one comparator while keeping duplicate records in their existing order when both keys match?

  • Are the timestamps already normalized to UTC? This matters for a date comparison. Jordan Nov 1 at 10:00
17

Compare the timestamps and return the result immediately when the timestamps differ. When they compare equal, compare the names and return that result. One comparator defines the complete order and makes the precedence of the fields explicit.

records.sort((a, b) => a.time - b.time || a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
Casey576
3

A sequence of stable sorts can work too. Sort by the less significant field first and then by the outer field. The second sort preserves the previous order within its groups, provided the sorting function is stable.
